extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and mathematics enthusiasts (AMS readers and potential subscribers/authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines/description for monthly AMS Feature Column essays: online pieces giving an in-depth look at a mathematical topic, illustrated and referenced, often with historical context and an enthusiastic author voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-depth look at a mathematical topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Each month, the Feature Column provides an online in-depth look at a mathematical topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays should treat a single mathematical topic at length, exploring it deeply rather than as a brief survey. (Page lists example topics such as 'Circles and Squares' and 'Knot Quandaries Quelled by Quandles' to illustrate scope.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete with graphics, links, and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete with graphics, links, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays are expected to include visual aids (graphics), hyperlinks for further reading or resources, and bibliographic references to support claims and direct interested readers to more detailed sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover a wide spectrum of mathematics and its applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The columns cover a wide spectrum of mathematics and its applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics may range across pure and applied mathematics; editors/authors should select subjects that demonstrate breadth across the discipline rather than focusing on a single subfield exclusively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include historical figures and their contributions (often)
rubrics_metrics.description: Often including historical figures and their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporating historical context and biographical material about mathematicians and their contributions is a common and encouraged element of the essays, to situate the mathematics culturally and historically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author voice: share excitement about developments in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors—David Austin, Bill Casselman, Joe Malkevitch, and Tony Phillips—share their excitement about developments in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays should convey enthusiasm and accessibility; an engaging, enthusiastic tone that communicates why the topic matters is part of the column's character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly online publication format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each month, the Feature Column provides an online ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series is a monthly online column; pieces should be prepared for web presentation and periodic (monthly) scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription availability (RSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscribe to an RSS feed for each new essay at ams.org/featurecolumn.rss
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are encouraged to subscribe via RSS; authors/editors should ensure feed-compatible metadata and timely publication so subscribers receive new essays.
